question: What is the total weight of the new feed I purchased in the past two months?

gold_sessions.user_turns:
[turn 0] I'm wondering if you can help me calculate the cost per pound of the layer feed I recently purchased. I got a 50-pound batch, and I'm trying to track my expenses for the farm.

[turn 2] I actually spent around $120 on the purchase, and I got a 10% discount from the local farm supply store.

[turn 4] I'm also thinking of adjusting the feeding schedule for my chickens, considering I've recently added two new hens to the flock. Do you have any general guidelines on how often to feed them and how much to give each day?

[turn 6] Can you give me some tips on how to transition my chickens to the new layer feed? I've heard that sudden changes can be stressful for them.

[turn 8] I'm also concerned about the quality of the eggs my girls are producing. Since I've added the new layer feed, I've noticed an improvement in the quality of the eggs, but I want to make sure I'm providing the best possible nutrition for them. Can you recommend any supplements or additional nutrients I can add to their diet to further improve egg quality?

[turn 10] I'm thinking of adding some homemade jam to my product line at the farmer's market. Can you give me some information on the regulations and permits required to sell homemade jam at a farmer's market?

[turn 0] I'm thinking of expanding my farm's product line to include homemade jam and honey. Can you help me find information on the regulations and permits required for selling these products at the local farmer's market? By the way, I also bought 20 pounds of organic scratch grains for my chickens recently, and I've noticed an improvement in the quality of eggs.

[turn 2] I have a few questions about the cottage food laws. Do I need to take a food safety certification course, or is it just recommended? And what kind of registration is required for selling jams and honey at the farmer's market - is it a one-time thing or do I need to renew it annually?

[turn 4] What about the labeling requirements for jams and honey? Do I need to include a nutrition facts label on my products, and are there any specific guidelines for labeling homemade products?

[turn 6] I see. So, I would need to include an ingredient list and allergen warning on my jam labels, but not a nutrition facts label. And for honey, I just need to include the net quantity and product name. Got it! By the way, I've been thinking of repurposing an old plow I found in the barn to use in the garden. Do you think that's a good idea, or should I just stick with modern gardening tools?

[turn 8] That's great to know! I think I'll give it a try and see how it works out. I've also been meaning to ask, do you have any tips on how to fix the fencing around the north pasture? I've got the materials ready, but I'm not sure where to start.
